about: Ground-truth capability labels for verifying the taxonomy in capabilities.py.
labelling_protocol: Labels record what a package's own documentation says it can do, read from its repository README and tool list.
Labels were assigned before running the taxonomy against them, and were not revised to improve any score.
No package was executed and no tarball was downloaded to produce these labels.
A capability is labelled present only when the documentation describes a tool that performs it. Inferred or plausible capabilities are left out, which makes recall the conservative direction.
Network access used solely to reach a service's own API is labelled net_egress only when the server can send caller-supplied content outward, not merely because a connection is opened.
Labels added 2026-09-06 were sourced from an independent documentation survey of each server's published tool list, conducted without reference to the taxonomy's output.
known_limitations: The set is small. It is large enough to expose a systematically broken rule and too small to estimate ecosystem-wide precision to a tight interval.
It is drawn from well-documented, widely-used servers, which are easier to label and probably cleaner than the ecosystem tail. Precision measured here is an optimistic bound.
Labels reflect documentation, which can be incomplete or aspirational relative to the code.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem
packages.basis: Documented tools read, write, edit, move files and list directories within allowed roots. No network tool is documented.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-github
packages.basis: Documented tools read file contents and search repositories, create or update files and branches, and create issues and pull requests. Issue and pull request bodies are attacker-writable content.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-gitlab
packages.basis: Documented tools mirror the GitHub server: read and write repository files, create branches, and create issues and merge requests.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack
packages.basis: Documented tools list channels, read channel and thread history, and post messages and replies. Message bodies are written by other people.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres
packages.basis: Documented as a read-only SQL query tool against a configured database. No write tool and no outbound content channel are documented.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search
packages.basis: Documented web and local search tools returning third-party page content and descriptions, which are attacker-plantable.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-puppeteer
packages.basis: Documented tools navigate to arbitrary URLs, screenshot, click, fill forms, and evaluate scripts in page context.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
packages.basis: Documented as a knowledge graph persisted to a local JSON file, which it both reads and writes. No network tool is documented.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking
packages.basis: Documented as a structured reasoning aid with no external access of any kind. Included deliberately as a negative control: a taxonomy that assigns this package any capability is producing false positives.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-google-maps
packages.basis: Documented tools query a mapping API for geocoding, places, and directions. Labelled conservatively: place data includes user-submitted text, but the server is not documented as a general content fetcher.

packages.name: firecrawl-mcp
packages.basis: Documented tools scrape arbitrary URLs, crawl sites, and return extracted page content as markdown.

packages.name: @upstash/context7-mcp
packages.basis: Documented tools resolve a library identifier and fetch that library's documentation text from a remote service.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-gdrive
packages.basis: Documented single search tool plus resource reads over the whole Drive account under a readonly OAuth scope, auto-converting Docs, Sheets and Slides to text. No write tool documented.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-redis
packages.basis: Documented tools set, get, delete and list against a configured Redis instance. Writes and deletes are unrestricted.

packages.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server-aws-kb-retrieval
packages.basis: Documented single retrieval tool against an AWS knowledge base, returning corpus documents. Configured with static AWS keys.

packages.name: @brave/brave-search-mcp-server
packages.basis: Documented web, local, video, image and news search tools plus a summarizer returning pre-extracted page content. No write tools documented.

packages.name: @playwright/mcp
packages.basis: Documented tools navigate, evaluate scripts, fill and submit forms, issue network requests, upload local files, and read cookies and storage state from a persistent authenticated browser profile.

packages.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
packages.basis: Documented browser automation, network request analysis and console inspection. Its own documentation states it exposes browser content to the client and permits modifying data in the browser.

packages.name: @notionhq/notion-mcp-server
packages.basis: Documented tools query and retrieve pages and data sources, and create or update pages, blocks and comments across the granted workspace.

packages.name: @supabase/mcp-server-supabase
packages.basis: Documented tools execute SQL, apply migrations, deploy edge functions and return publishable API keys. Read-only mode is opt-in.

packages.name: tavily-mcp
packages.basis: Documented search, extract, map and crawl tools returning third-party web content.

packages.name: exa-mcp-server
packages.basis: Documented web search and an arbitrary-URL fetch tool.

packages.name: mongodb-mcp-server
packages.basis: Documented database tools find, aggregate, export, insert, update and drop, plus Atlas control-plane tools that create database users and modify the network access list.
